html:
Ali-Shir Nava'i was a poet and statesman at Herat, the last great capital of the Timurid Empire. He is the greatest writer in Chagatai, the Turkic literary language of Central Asia.

He grew up with the future sultan Husayn Bayqara and served him as a minister and close friend. Most educated people then wrote poetry in Persian. Nava'i argued that Turkic was just as fit for fine writing, and in 1499 he set out the case in The Comparison of the Two Languages. He proved it with thousands of poems and a Turkic Khamsa, five long verse tales after the Persian model.

He was also a great patron. He paid for mosques, schools, hospitals and bridges, and supported artists such as the painter Behzad and the poet Jami. Babur, who also wrote in Chagatai, praised him in his memoirs. Uzbeks today honour him as their national poet.
sum: Ali-Shir Nava'i was a poet and statesman at Herat, the last great capital of the Timurid Empire. He is the greatest writer in Chagatai, the Turkic literary language of Central Asia.
